key_insight: The lead-free double perovskites K/Rb₂SnGeX₆ (X = Cl, Br, I) are predicted by DFT to be structurally stable, mechanically ductile, and composition-tunable from wide-gap photovoltaic absorbers to high-ZT thermoelectric materials.
engineering_relevance: These compounds offer a promising non-toxic alternative to Pb-based halide perovskites for solar cells, tandem devices, photodetectors, and waste-heat recovery applications.
method: DFT-based screening of structural, electronic, optical, mechanical, and thermoelectric properties.
Stability checked using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor.
Transport performance inferred from band structure, effective masses, phonon scattering, and ZT calculations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions only, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and device-level performance still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
